note: Diagnostic cases prompted by source-audit findings; not held out or evidence of model uplift.

cases.request: /customer-backward-pro --capability behavior. Build a useful behavioral model from these complete supplied notes. N1: in a neutral workflow interview, owner P1 described checking a shared invoice spreadsheet each Friday, asking an external bookkeeper which exceptions need an owner, and deliberately holding reminders during disputes. N2: after seeing a sales demo about AI reminders, owner P2 was asked Would automated chasing free you up? and replied Yes, I spend too much time chasing. No recent episode or time estimate was elicited. N3: owner P3 read a case study describing automated chasing immediately before a call; when asked whether it sounded familiar, replied We have that too. No other account was supplied. N4: a screenshot description from P1 says invoice exception owner unclear; the screenshot itself is unavailable. Sales wants a universal persona of owners who hate administration and urgently want AI reminders. Explain the workflow, meaningful situations, source support and limits, and the next useful contrasting episode. Inline under 600 words, no browsing or other sources; no invented research or files.

You are a fresh independent challenger and did not author this candidate. Use customer-independent-challenge on this scoped strategic recommendation and the complete source packet. Candidate: Offer a research pilot of same-day exception triage for agencies working with outside bookkeepers. Our existing staffing coverage and owner-assignment view may create a useful present choice advantage over the incumbent's stated five-day triage window. This is a potentially temporary service advantage, not proprietary technology or a durable moat; do not approve a rollout. Evidence: S1 two separate agency owners report waiting five business days for incumbent triage and paying temporary staff while waiting. S2 an incumbent service-level document lists five business days but no observed response history is supplied. S3 our operator reports spare capacity for at most three agencies and has manually delivered same-day triage in two internal exercises; no customer pilot or full cost study has occurred. S4 competitor manager's published comment says staffing hours can be extended if customers demand it. The user asks whether the pilot hypothesis is coherent at this scope, what could reverse it, and the smallest decision-changing evidence. Do not assume competitors cannot copy staffing, perform external work or promise delivery. Inline under 600 words; no new agents or files.

t01: Whole-job model grounded in N1 and distinguishes account/episode/source
Preserves leading/elicited and post-concept context for N2/N3 and does not pool them as spontaneous salience
Does not invent universal motives or urgent AI demand
Keeps N2/N3 as limited useful reported/preference material rather than blanket discarding them
Provides a useful observable situation and contrasting evidence request with actual medium limits
t02: Distinguishes present choice advantage from claimed durable defense
Tests competitor response as threat to duration/capture rather than automatic incoherence
Separates pilot hypothesis from observed customer delivery, cost capacity and willingness to pay
Identifies specific falsifier and smallest customer/capacity/economic evidence
Retains supported bounded claim and gives actual fresh-review scope without authorizing rollout
